findings.title: Secret hardcoded in environment
findings.risk: Credentials written in the compose file end up in version control and are visible to anyone who can read the file or inspect the container.
findings.fix: Use an env_file kept out of version control, Docker secrets, or variable references such as ${DB_PASSWORD}.

findings.title: No non-root user set for the service
findings.risk: The service may run as root. This is a false alarm only if the image itself already sets a non-root USER.
findings.fix: Set "user" to an unprivileged UID:GID, for example user "1001:1001", after checking file permissions.

findings.title: no-new-privileges not set
findings.risk: Without it, processes in the container can gain extra privileges through setuid binaries, which helps an attacker escalate.
findings.fix: Add "security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]" to the service.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.evidence: no USER instruction, container runs as root
findings.risk: Without a non-root USER, the application runs as root inside the container. If an attacker exploits the app, they start with full privileges, which makes container escape and file tampering easier.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user and switch to it, for example "RUN useradd -r -u 1001 app" then "USER app".

findings.title: No HEALTHCHECK defined
findings.risk: Without a health check, Docker cannot tell that the app has hung or failed, so broken containers can keep serving traffic.
findings.fix: Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction that tests the application, for example an HTTP request to a status endpoint.

findings.risk: Without a non-root USER, the application runs as root inside the container. If an attacker exploits the app, they start with full privileges, which makes container escape and file tampering easier.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user and switch to it, for example "RUN useradd -r -u 1001 app" then "USER app".

findings.title: No HEALTHCHECK defined
findings.risk: Without a health check, Docker cannot tell that the app has hung or failed, so broken containers can keep serving traffic.
findings.fix: Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction that tests the application, for example an HTTP request to a status endpoint.

findings.title: Remote script piped into a shell
findings.risk: Running a downloaded script without checking it executes whatever the server returns at build time, including malicious changes.
findings.fix: Download the file, verify its checksum or signature, then run it in a separate step.
